name: LP-EM-CC35X1 LaunchPad development kit
sources: CC3551E data sheet SWRS337B (June 2026; core, memory, radio, currents); LaunchPad user guide SWRU629C rev C, April 2026 (jumpers, LEDs, buttons, power, antenna, Figures 2-1, 2-17, 2-25); SimpleLink Wi-Fi SDK 10.20.00.39 release notes and board file LP_EM_CC35X1.syscfg.json; all read 2026-10-07

columns.head: The chip: CC3551E
items: Processor: Arm Cortex-M33
Runs your program at up to 160 MHz, with a floating-point unit
RAM: 1.1 MB
Shared by Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, the network stack and your program
Flash: outside the chip
The program runs from an 8 MB QSPI flash chip through a 32 or 64 kB cache
Radio: Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth LE 5.4
Wi-Fi on 2.4 and 5 GHz, up to 20.5 dBm; transmit draws up to 310 mA at 3.3 V

columns.head: Connections inside the chip
items: GPIO: up to 36
On/off pins; most go to the two 20-pin headers
UART: 3
UART1 goes to the probe's serial port; UART0 is free on header pins 3 and 4
SPI: 2 / I2C: 2 / CAN / SD
Displays, sensors, a car-style bus, a memory card
ADC: 12-bit, 8 channels
Measures voltages; four go through buffers on this board

columns.head: On the board, and missing
items: On the board
RGB LED, two buttons, reset, temperature sensor, accelerometer, USB-C for power
Antenna
Chip antenna. The SMA (J1) and U.FL (J2) need a capacitor moved first
Not on the board
No debug probe: it needs the LP-XDS110ET (or LP-XDS110) for flashing
Watch out
Two USB cables to the same Mac: the probe's and the board's own USB-C
